P1.evidence: Setter acknowledged but not read back: 'already got some information from Kim as well. But we just like to hear everything from you.' Nothing specific was reflected. The frame covered two of four parts — 'we're just going to go where you're at, where you want to go' — plus the fit outcome. Agreement obtained. Open question asked verbatim.

P2.evidence: P2d ran twice and properly: 'other things that you feel like are sort of coming up here and there, maybe some aches or pains overall throughout today or not really?' then 'Any stiffnesses that we should know about?' Training reality was pinned down precisely (three to four times a week, 30-60 minutes, wake time dependent). Nutrition was probed to the weekend slip. But age was volunteered rather than asked, height and weight were never asked, health conditions were never asked, sleep was never asked, and energy was raised only as a suggested motive rather than as a baseline question.

P3.evidence: The bridge question was asked and produced the single best answer in the batch: 'is there a reason for you to why you want to, well, start focusing on your mobility now more?' — 'I've got parents that never moved and I saw them get old and like crumble. So I don't want that to happen to me.' The rep summarised it as 'a preventative longevity aspect' and then let it go. P3f is the decisive miss: a wife and a two-year-old daughter were both mentioned in the first ninety seconds and neither was ever connected to the goal. The wife then reappeared at 00:34:48 as the obstacle.

P4.evidence: P4d and P4e both landed. 'what is it that you would actually want to see from us in order to be like, okay, this is actually something I see myself working with?' produced the real gap, and the prospect named it precisely: 'if I've got someone who's kind of counting on me to do it, I think having someone holding me accountable, I think that's going to help me push through that.' He then volunteered that he skips cardio days out of dread — 'I sometimes get scared on cardio days. I'm like, oh, I don't want to be out of breath. So you don't do it' — and the rep answered 'Yeah, getting the accountability' and moved on without once asking why.

P5.evidence: Entirely skipped, and this is the headline failure of the call. The prospect had already supplied the exact image Phase 5 exists to build — his parents never moving, getting old and crumbling — and was never asked what happens if nothing changes, whether he is willing to settle for it, or why not. The strongest consequence material in the batch was handed over and left on the table.

P6.evidence: P6b ran cleanly: 'do you feel like there might be something internally that would stop you from committing 100 percent?' Notably the prospect offered the capacity test himself — 'I mean, are you talking about financially?' — and the rep declined it: 'No, no, no.' Commitment was therefore secured on execution only, and the money question the prospect had raised was actively deferred until after the presentation.

P11.evidence: No close was attempted. No payment was requested and no link was sent; the call ended on a follow-up date.

objection_plays.detail: Unambiguous trigger: 'I need to double-track until I talk to my wife, because that's a big number, grand isn't nothing.' Not one of the six scripted moves ran. No 'money aside, do you personally feel this can get you to your goal', no 'when you talk to her, what obstacles might come up', no 'is there any reason she would not want you stronger', no 'is this genuinely needing her input or asking permission to bet on yourself', no deposit-and-discuss. The rep did not acknowledge the sentence at all and continued on price.

The worth-it test ran — 'would you feel like that is worth the 4K for you or also not really?' — and the price was justified via Trevor's demand. Nothing else. No isolation before the money question, no cash on hand, no monthly leftover, no credit cards, no available credit, no investments. When the prospect named $2,000 the rep answered with cheaper products rather than with the play.

Trigger: 'Why don't you send me a follow-up, and then I'll let you know.' One genuinely good non-scripted move ran — a one-to-ten scale that isolated the gap to price alone ('the seven and a half, seven is, is that like the price points, those two and a half points? Yeah, yeah') and a control question separating programme from price. None of the scripted OA moves ran, and no attempt was made to convert the isolated price gap into a decision.

Two script gaps. First, a live competitive process — 'I've got some calls scheduled next week with some other trainers' and 'the other programs I've seen were a little less' — with no scripted play for defending against a comparison shopper. Second, a value-at-reduced-scope objection: 'I'm looking for like a fine-tune, and I think your program is more for somebody who needs a lot more than I do.' The rep answered the second by discounting the product rather than repositioning the value.

notes: One correction outweighs everything else here: the prospect volunteered watching his parents get old and crumble, which is the consequence frame ready-made, and Phase 5 was never run. Second: a wife and a two-year-old daughter were mentioned in the first ninety seconds, never used in Phase 3, and the wife then became the blocking objection which was not acknowledged at all. Third: when the prospect offered to discuss money at the commitment check, the rep waved it off, and four different prices then appeared in the following eight minutes.
